Survival Curve for the G2G Model with Time-Invariant Covariates

Source: R/G2G_static_functions.R
G2G_static_survival.Rd

Computes the survival curve implied by a fitted static G2G model for one set of covariate values: \(S(t) = (1 + t \cdot \exp(\mathbf{x}'\boldsymbol{\beta}) / \alpha)^{-r}\), with \(S(0) = 1\).

Usage

G2G_static_survival(solution, X_vect, timeperiod)

Arguments

solution

A fitted model of class "G2Gcov" returned by G2G_static_MLE. Its par holds r, alpha and the coefficients on the original covariate scale (alpha already absorbs the centering used in fitting), so X_vect needs no centering or scaling.

X_vect

Covariate values for one subject. Only one set of values is accepted per call; to get curves for several subjects or covariate profiles, call the function once per profile (for example in a loop or with sapply). Either a one-row data frame containing the original covariate variables (factors and dummy variables are coded as in the fit, using the stored terms and factor levels; a missing value is an error), or plain numbers: one value per model coefficient, as a numeric vector or one-row matrix named like the coefficients (any order) or unnamed in the same order as the coefficients. If the model has a single covariate coefficient, a single number. Anything else (more than one row, or the wrong number of values) is an error.

timeperiod

Number of periods, a whole number >= 1. The curve is returned for periods 0, 1, ..., timeperiod.

Value

Numeric vector of length timeperiod + 1 with the survival probabilities S(0) = 1, S(1), ..., S(timeperiod).

Examples

# \donttest{
  if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) {
    library(survival)
    fit <- G2G_static_MLE(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno, data = veteran)
    G2G_static_survival(fit, data.frame(age = 60, karno = 70),
                        timeperiod = 30)
  }
#>  [1] 1.0000000 0.9928962 0.9858521 0.9788670 0.9719403 0.9650716 0.9582602
#>  [8] 0.9515057 0.9448073 0.9381647 0.9315773 0.9250445 0.9185658 0.9121407
#> [15] 0.9057687 0.8994494 0.8931821 0.8869664 0.8808018 0.8746878 0.8686240
#> [22] 0.8626098 0.8566449 0.8507286 0.8448607 0.8390405 0.8332678 0.8275419
#> [29] 0.8218626 0.8162293 0.8106416
# }
